blocks.md: This lesson covers the book's section on **Physical Channels of the Sim-to-Real Gap**. Read the excerpt, then test yourself below.

blocks.source: Vol IV, Policy Training, § Physical Channels of the Sim-to-Real Gap
blocks.md: A robotic simulation rarely diverges from physical hardware in only one channel. In the cage-door latch mechanism, for instance, the simulator departs from reality in two different ways: a penalty spring far softer than the physical strike plate, and an idealized command path that omits transport lag. Collapsing these discrepancies into a single scalar trajectory error blends them into an uninformative aggregate that obscures both mechanisms. Errors in different physical channels carry different units, propagate along distinct paths within the closed loop, and trigger different failure modes.

questions.q: The section **Physical Channels of the Sim-to-Real Gap** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: Sim-to-real mismatch decomposes into dynamics, sensing, appearance, and timing channels, each sized by paired probing, and randomization covers modeled parameters but never omitted mechanisms.
State value, action value, advantage, and the Bellman relation express value as negated cost-to-go, with LQR as the closed-form linear-quadratic case.
Chunked imitation fits a horizon of actions with a Huber penalty on normalized residuals, which buys outlier robustness, not smoothness or feasibility.
A trial campaign's wall clock is trials times rollout plus reset over rigs (about 93 days of execution for 10^6 latch trials before resets), and every trial spends heat and drivetrain life.
